title: Hub Cafe
venue_description:
Hub Cafe Overview

Hub Cafe is a unique farmer-owned restaurant that has been serving the Lincoln community since January 2016. Located at the scenic Jayne Snyder Trails Center in Lincoln's Telegraph District the cafe is owned and operated by Branched Oak Farm and maintains a strong commitment to sourcing local ingredients for their menu.

Farm-to-Table Philosophy

The cafe is rooted in community connections and sustainable food sourcing. They work directly with local growers and small farms in Lincoln and the surrounding area to provide the freshest ingredients. This commitment allows them to serve the freshest best-tasting produce dairy products and meat to inspire creative dishes. The menu features unique breakfast and lunch options made from local eggs meat dairy and produce.

Live Music and Events

Hub Cafe has become a cornerstone of Lincoln's live music scene hosting open mic nights on the first and third Thursday of each month from 5-8pm. These events are presented in partnership with Roots Music Shop who sponsor the equipment setup. The open mic welcomes musicians singers comedians and poets and always concludes with a large jam session. Chefs Jake and Kelley provide a rotating monthly menu of pizza and small bites to enjoy during performances.

The venue also participates in Hub and Soul a free community event designed for people of all ages and backgrounds to celebrate music local food and Lincoln's parks. These events are held on select dates throughout the summer months at the nearby Union Plaza Amphitheatre.

Friday Night Live Music

Every Friday night the Hub Cafe features live local music with a rotating monthly menu of creative pizzas and small bites creating a vibrant atmosphere to start the weekend. The combination of quality local food and live performances has made Friday nights a popular destination in the Telegraph District.

The Space and Accessibility

Located at the Jayne Snyder Trails Center at 250 N 21st Street Suite 3 the cafe offers beautiful views overlooking the Antelope Valley. The venue is easily accessible being walkable bikeable and offering car parking. The Jayne Snyder Trails Center is also available for private events outside regular business hours making it a versatile space for celebrations and gatherings.

Menu and Dining Experience

Hub Cafe serves breakfast and lunch with menu items ranging from simple classics like eggs sausage and potatoes to more adventurous dishes like the Hub Skillet featuring goat cheese chorizo and kale. The emphasis on fresh local ingredients means the menu showcases seasonal offerings and creative preparations that change regularly.

title: Zoo Bar
venue_description:
Zoo Bar Overview

The Zoo Bar is a legendary blues music venue and nightclub located in downtown Lincoln Nebraska at 136 North 14th Street. Housed in a building constructed in 1921 and styled after the Chicago blues clubs the Zoo is a long narrow venue that has been the heartbeat of Lincoln's live music scene since 1973.

Rich History

Around 1971 Jim Ludwig Bill Kennedy and Don Chamberlin purchased the bar. Larry Boehmer a Master of Fine Arts student at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln at the time promoted the bar to his fellow artists and booked the first band in 1973. By 1977 Boehmer was the sole owner. He formed a crucial connection with Chicago musician and promoter Bob Riedy which brought many revered Chicago artists to the Lincoln club.

The Zoo Bar holds the distinction of being the first white club that Magic Slim ever played. In 1975 he had never ventured outside the clubs in Chicago's African-American neighborhoods. Magic Slim and his band became regular performers playing week-long stints and in the 1990s Magic Slim moved his family from Chicago to Lincoln.

In 1993 the Zoo Bar won the Blues Foundation's Keeping the Blues Alive Award for Club of the Year. In 2000 Larry Boehmer retired and passed the bar to his sons Jeff and Tim Boehmer and Pete Watters. Currently Jeff Boehmer and Pete Watters are partners in the club. Larry Boehmer passed away in September 2012 after struggling with lung cancer and is remembered as a visual artist blues bass player and community builder.

The Jazzocracy - Weekly Jazz Jam

Every Tuesday night at 6pm the Zoo Bar hosts The Jazzocracy Lincoln's longest running weekly jazz jam session. The event is open to students and jazz musicians who want to jam or for anyone who wants to listen. The sessions feature a wide variety of modern and classic jazz compositions with no cover charge. Among the regular hosts are Bill Wimmer on saxophone Aaron Stroessner on guitar Brian Gerkensmeyer on bass and Parker Sibley on drums. The night continues after the jam session with DJ Relic spinning soul music until morning.

Other Regular Programming

The Zoo Bar offers live music six to seven nights a week with a variety of recurring events. Monday nights feature Emily Bass and friends playing up close and personal next to the bar taking requests from 5:30 to 7:30pm with no cover charge. The first Sunday of each month hosts an afternoon jam session from 2-5pm where solo performers and group performances are welcome. Accompaniment is available for those who need it and performers are encouraged to bring simple lead sheets with chords. Sets run 15-20 minutes depending on attendance.

Thursdays feature Shithook Live Band Karaoke where audience members pick songs and the live band plays them. Every other Wednesday night hosts Vibe Check a soulful groovy moody event with no cover charge that continues to elevate with each show.

ZooFest - Annual Celebration

ZooFest is the Zoo Bar's mid-summer anniversary celebration that spills into the street transforming 14th Street into the stage. The festival brings famous jazz and blues musicians for a day of outdoor performances. The 2024 celebration marked the venue's 51st anniversary continuing a tradition that has made ZooFest one of Lincoln's most anticipated annual music events.

Legendary Performers

Over its five decades the Zoo Bar has hosted an incredible roster of blues and roots music legends. The list includes Bernard Allison Luther Allison Dave Alvin Tab Benoit Tommy Castro Albert Collins Robert Cray Bo Diddley Buddy Guy John Hammond Candye Kane Charlie Musselwhite Rod Piazza Ana Popovic Otis Rush Koko Taylor Junior Wells Kim Wilson Link Wray Eddie Clearwater Mighty Joe Young Clarence Gatemouth Brown Carey Bell and The Blind Boys of Alabama among many others.

James Harman wrote a song on behalf of the club called Everybody's Rockin' At The Zoo Bar which can be found on Harman's 1995 Black and White CD cementing the venue's place in blues music history.

The Venue Experience

The intimate setting features a low stage wood floors and walls lined with show posters that tell decades of musical stories. The warm punchy sound system and close connection to performers turns concerts into conversations. Most nights are general admission with standing room near the stage and some bar stools along the perimeter. The Zoo opens daily at 3:00pm and offers quick bar service and a friendly atmosphere.

While the Zoo Bar does not serve food guests are welcome to bring in food from the many great restaurants in the surrounding area. The venue offers a full bar service.

Location and Accessibility

Located just a half block off O Street in the heart of downtown Lincoln the Zoo Bar sits within easy walking distance of restaurants bars and the University of Nebraska campus making pre-show plans simple. The downtown location has made it a gathering place for students locals and music lovers from across the region for over 50 years.

title: Night Owl Pub
venue_description:
Night Owl Pub Overview

Night Owl Pub is a neighborhood pub-style bar located in south Lincoln at 3233 S 13th Street. The venue offers a spot for people who want to escape the crowd and try new drinks in a comfortable welcoming atmosphere. The pub has established itself as an important venue for Lincoln's live music community particularly through its weekly open mic night.

Open Mic Night

Every Wednesday from 8pm to 1am Night Owl Pub hosts Lincoln Open Mic Night one of the city's most welcoming and inclusive music events. The event is hosted by Jackie Storm and has built a reputation as a music family that welcomes music lovers of all types with open arms to come and enjoy as well as participate in Lincoln's local live music scene.

The venue provides comprehensive support for performers including a PA system sound engineer DI boxes microphones and occasionally allows sharing of drum kits and other instruments. All genres are welcome making it a truly inclusive space for diverse musical expression from rock and blues to folk acoustic and experimental music.

Sign Up and Participation

Performers interested in playing at the open mic can sign up through the Lincoln Open Mic Night Facebook page. For each date there is an event posted and under the Discussion section performers can comment to request a time slot. The sign up sheet is updated continuously as people reserve their spots making it easy to plan ahead.

The event operates with a mission to hold a creative space for the gathering growth and enjoyment of local musicians and singer-songwriters. It serves as both a performance opportunity and a networking hub where musicians can connect collaborate and support each other's artistic development.

Atmosphere and Offerings

Night Owl Pub describes itself as a neighborhood pub that maintains a safe atmosphere for all ages over 21. The drink menu features specialty cocktails including martinis mules mojitos and house-made infusions providing creative options beyond standard bar fare. The intimate setting allows for close connection between performers and audience members creating a supportive environment for both seasoned artists and those just starting out.

Hours and Accessibility

The pub is open Tuesday through Sunday from 5pm to 2am and is closed on Mondays. The south Lincoln location at 3233 S 13th Street offers parking and easy access for both performers and audience members coming from different parts of the city.

title: Bourbon Theatre
venue_description:
Bourbon Theatre Overview

The Bourbon Theatre opened in 2009 and has established itself as a premier music venue in Nebraska's capital city. Located at 1415 O Street in downtown Lincoln the venue is housed in a completely remodeled 1920 movie theatre that has undergone numerous renovations and upgrades to become one of the most sought-after clubs in the Midwest.

The Venue

Originally a turn-of-the-century movie theater the Bourbon Theatre has been transformed into a state-of-the-art music venue while maintaining architectural charm from its theatrical past. The vintage marquee at 1415 O Street has become an iconic landmark announcing upcoming acts and drawing music fans from across the region.

With the ability to host events both large and small the Bourbon provides a unique and intimate space to see live performances. The venue features professional sound and lighting systems that can accommodate everything from acoustic singer-songwriters to full rock bands and electronic acts.

Open Mic Monday

Every Monday at 8pm the Bourbon Theatre hosts open mic night which continues until close. The event is open to all facets of music and has an 18+ age requirement. Special time slots are set aside for featured local and touring acts making it both a platform for emerging artists and a showcase for more established performers passing through Lincoln.

The open mic takes advantage of the venue's professional sound system and stage setup giving performers a chance to play on the same stage that hosts national touring acts throughout the week.

Diverse Music Programming

The Bourbon Theatre's calendar features an incredibly diverse range of musical genres and events. Whether fans are into rock country rap blues alternative indie or anything in between there is consistently something on the schedule. Recent and upcoming performances have included national acts across all genres as well as regional favorites and local bands.

The venue has hosted everyone from punk and metal bands to country artists hip-hop performers and tribute acts. This eclecticism has made the Bourbon a cornerstone of Lincoln's music scene appealing to a wide demographic of music lovers.

Bar and Atmosphere

True to its name the Bourbon Theatre features a bar stocked with a wide variety of whiskeys along with a full selection of beer wine and cocktails. The bartending staff is experienced and the bar service is efficient even during sold-out shows. The venue's layout allows for good sightlines from various positions whether guests are near the stage at the bar or in the back of the room.

Location and Access

Situated in downtown Lincoln just a few blocks from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln campus the Bourbon Theatre is a pillar in the bustling O Street corridor. The location puts it in the heart of Lincoln's entertainment district surrounded by bars restaurants retail shops and other nightlife options.

The downtown location makes it easily accessible for students and residents alike. The area offers various parking options including street parking and nearby parking garages. The proximity to other venues and establishments means concert-goers can easily make a night of it exploring the downtown area before or after shows.

Box Office and Ticketing

The Bourbon Theatre box office is open Tuesday through Friday from 11am to 5pm. Tickets for events can be purchased in person during these hours through the venue's website or through various ticketing platforms. Many shows are all-ages though some events including the weekly open mic have age restrictions.
